title: Headway Vendor Adapter Trip-Resolution Spec v0
description: The machine-validated format of adapters/<vendor>/<product>/resolution.v0.yaml (handoff 0031): declarative, PER-AGENCY configuration for resolving a vendor export's own trip and stop identifiers against the agency's GTFS schedule already normalized into canonical.trips / canonical.stops. A vendor APC export names a trip in the agency's operational vocabulary ('route - pattern - start time'); the GTFS trip_id is usually an opaque id. Nothing in this format is agency-specific code: how the vendor's trip name is taken apart, which GTFS field each part matches, the direction convention, and the service-day rollover convention are all DECLARED here and confirmed by the agency. The resolver has exactly three outcomes - resolved (exactly one scheduled trip matches), ambiguous (more than one), unmatched (none) - and the last two become data-quality findings that name what was parsed and what was searched. It never picks a candidate. Prose companion: contracts/adapter-resolution.v0.md.

resolution_spec_version.description: Format version. v0 resolves TIDES passenger_events rows produced by a sibling mapping.v0.yaml.

source_label.description: MUST equal the source_label of the mapping.v0.yaml next to this file. The registry pairs the two by label and refuses a mismatch rather than resolve one vendor's rows with another's configuration.

target_contract.description: The contract whose records this spec resolves. v0 supports tides_passenger_events only: it is the contract that carries a performed-trip identifier.

trip.description: How the vendor's own trip identifier becomes (at most) one canonical trip_id.

vendor_identifier.description: WHERE the vendor's trip identifier is read from. Exactly one of from_field (a target field the sibling mapping spec fills, e.g. trip_id_performed) or from_column (a raw source column of the vendor file).

from_field.description: A target contract field the sibling mapping spec maps. Spec load fails if the mapping spec does not map it.

from_column.description: A raw source column of the vendor file. For headerless formats it must be one of the mapping spec's declared positional columns.

parse.description: How the vendor identifier is taken apart. v0 splits on a literal separator into a fixed, named component list. A value that does not split into EXACTLY that many parts is UNMATCHED with the reason stated - a partial parse is never guessed at.

separator.description: Literal separator, used verbatim (e.g. ' - '). Not a regular expression.

components.description: Names for the split parts, in order. Every part is named even when the resolver does not match on it (e.g. a pattern name), so an unmatched finding can state the whole parse.

strip.description: Strip surrounding whitespace from each component before matching.

match.description: The join key. All four clauses are REQUIRED in v0 and that is a measured decision, not a stylistic one: on the first agency's live feed (2,704 trips) the key (service, route short name, start time) collided on 500 keys covering 1,000 trips - 37% ambiguous - while adding direction left 1 collision covering 2 trips. Dropping service is worse still (823 colliding keys, 1,816 trips). A weaker key does not resolve; it manufactures ambiguity.

component.description: Which parsed component carries the route. Must be one of trip.parse.components.

gtfs_field.description: The canonical.routes field the component is compared against, verbatim and case-sensitively. Declared because the two are NOT interchangeable across agencies (they happen to be identical in the first agency's feed; that coincidence is never assumed).

component.description: Which parsed component carries the trip's scheduled start time. Must be one of trip.parse.components.

format.description: strptime format of that component (e.g. '%H:%M'). A component that does not parse makes the row UNMATCHED with the reason stated.

direction.description: The vendor's direction vocabulary mapped onto GTFS direction_id. A DIRECTION IS NEVER ASSUMED: GTFS itself assigns no meaning to 0 and 1 (the Schedule Reference calls them e.g. outbound/inbound only as an example), so which vendor value means which is an agency fact, not a convention this software may infer.

from_column.description: The raw source column carrying the vendor's direction key. For headerless formats it must be one of the mapping spec's declared positional columns.

confirmed.description: TRUE only when the agency has confirmed which vendor value corresponds to which GTFS direction_id. While FALSE the resolver RESOLVES NOTHING for this source and says so once per file - refusing is the specified behaviour, because a 50/50 guess on direction attaches passenger counts to the wrong trip half the time and nothing downstream would notice.

values.description: Vendor direction value (as it appears in the file, whitespace-stripped) -> GTFS direction_id. A value with no entry makes the row UNMATCHED with the reason stated; vendor vocabulary is mapped explicitly, never guessed.

confirmed_by.description: Who at the agency confirmed the mapping, and against what. REQUIRED when confirmed is true.

confirmed_on.description: When the mapping was confirmed. REQUIRED when confirmed is true.

unconfirmed_reason.description: Why the mapping is not yet confirmed and exactly what the agency must confirm. REQUIRED when confirmed is false; surfaced verbatim in the DQ finding that explains why nothing resolved.

service.description: Which service day the export row belongs to. Candidate trips are restricted to the GTFS services active on that day (calendar.txt + calendar_dates.txt, normalized into canonical.service_calendars / canonical.service_calendar_dates).

from_field.description: The target field carrying the row's service date (e.g. service_date). Must be a field the sibling mapping spec maps.

service_day_rollover.description: How the export dates a trip that runs past midnight. 'calendar_date' declares that the export's date is the CALENDAR date, so a GTFS trip whose scheduled start is at or past 24:00:00 belongs to the PREVIOUS service date and is matched there. 'not_confirmed' means the convention has not been established from a real export spanning midnight: the resolver then matches only within the calendar date and against GTFS start times before 24:00:00, and reports anything that would need the other reading as UNMATCHED with the reason stated.

stop.description: Optional. Checks the export's stop identifier against the agency's GTFS stops. v0 RESOLVES NOTHING ONTO THE ROW - the canonical passenger_events subset carries no stop-identity column (handoff 0011's open gap) - it exists so a stop the schedule does not know becomes a finding instead of a silence.

from_column.description: The raw source column carrying the vendor's stop identifier.

match_order.description: Which canonical.stops fields to check, in order, first hit wins. Declared per agency: an agency whose stop_id happens to equal its stop_code must not turn that coincidence into an assumption.

provenance.description: REQUIRED provenance of the CONFIGURATION - what schedule feed its key was measured against, and whether a real vendor export has ever been run through it. A resolution spec that has never met the vendor's real export is a legitimate artifact; pretending otherwise is not.

schedule_feed.description: The agency's GTFS feed the join key's uniqueness was MEASURED against - not assumed from the format's shape.

trips.description: How many trips the measured feed contained.

key_uniqueness.description: The measured result of applying this spec's join key to that feed, in numbers (how many keys collided, how many trips they covered).

vendor_export.description: Whether this configuration has ever been run against the vendor's REAL export.

status.description: none_available: no real export exists yet - the spec was exercised against synthetic rows in the export's proven shape. sample: verified against an agency-provided sample. production: verified against a real production delivery.

note.description: What was actually run through the spec, and what remains unverified because of it.

verification_date.description: When this spec was last verified (the run date of the evidence above).

notes.description: Free-text provenance notes. Same BINDING rule as the mapping spec: must NOT quote, excerpt, cite, or paraphrase vendor documentation.
